questions.title: Who will win the lightweight co-main event at UFC 331?
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : UFC's official results or contemporaneous reporting of the lightweight co-main event at UFC 331, scheduled for September 19, 2026. questions.current_reasoning: Major update on Aug 1 as UFC officially announced UFC 331 for Sept 19 at Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles (tickets on sale Aug 7) and multiple independent MMA reporters (Manouk Akopyan, Leo Guimaraes, RedFuryMMA, Bloody Elbow, AgentMMA) report Arman Tsarukyan (#2 LW) vs Charles Oliveira (#3 LW, BMF holder) is set as a 5-round non-title lightweight bout alongside the confirmed Joshua Van (c) vs Alexandre Pantoja 2 flyweight title fight (with Harrison vs Nunes postponed). Tsarukyan (29, beat Oliveira via split decision at UFC 300, submitted Dan Hooker in Nov 2025) is roughly a 65-67% favorite over Oliveira (36, beat Holloway in March 2026) over 5 rounds. Respecting pre-official-announcement uncertainty (UFC has not formally published the bout order), billing risk (if Tsarukyan-Oliveira headlines), and 7-week injury/weight-cut withdrawal risk (~15%, notably Tsarukyan's Jan 2025 UFC 311 LA back-injury pullout), Arman Tsarukyan rises 0.19 -> 0.48 (capped below 0.50 until official UFC confirmation) and Charles Oliveira rises 0.14 -> 0.26. Renato Moicano (0.05) and Brian Ortega (0.03) enter top 5 because their lightweight bout is already confirmed for UFC 331 (making them prime promotion/short-notice replacement candidates, as Moicano did at UFC 311), with Mauricio Ruffy trimmed 0.10 -> 0.03 (sum = 0.85, 15% residual for other replacements/matchups).

questions.title: Which DRC province will WHO identify as experiencing a surge in weekly Ebola cases in mid-September 2026?
questions.background: The Democratic Republic of Congo declared an Ebola outbreak in May 2026.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : WHO public statements about the DRC Ebola outbreak, including statements quoted in contemporaneous reputable news reporting. Resolution Window : Resolve to the province explicitly identified by WHO as experiencing surging weekly Ebola cases in its outbreak assessment publicly reported between September 10 and September 16, 2026. Accepted Answer Format : The name of the province.
questions.current_reasoning: Hard provincial data from WHO Disease Outbreak News DON614 (Aug 1, data to July 30), DRC INSP SitRep 079 (published Aug 2, data to Aug 1, via beto.cd Aug 3), and Aug 4 Reuters/AFP/UN News/Al Jazeera updates (national toll now 3,802 cases and 1,707 deaths—DRC's largest ever and world's second-largest): (1) North Kivu strengthens as #1 (0.35 -> 0.40) after climbing +27.4% in 6 days from 314 to 400 cases (262 deaths, 65.5% CFR; 7/11 daily deaths in community) while holding 5,667 contacts under follow-up—an astonishing 31.7% of all contacts nationwide despite only 10.7% of cumulative cases! Bed occupancy remains 128.4%, non-Ituri provinces rose to 33.8% of Aug 1 daily confirmations, and community resistance escalated sharply (Crinovic hospital & Zawadi health post burned in Butembo July 28-30, safe burial blocked July 31, Beni ambulance stoned Aug 1, Butembo anti-curfew protests Aug 3)—prime setup for a mid-September WHO weekly surge call. (2) Ituri trims 0.31 -> 0.28: still the epicentre at 3,278 cases (+13.0% in 6d, 11,638 contacts) with unpaid worker protests in Bunia/Rwampara/Mongbwalu and a Niania helipad/ETC attack Aug 4, but its share of daily confirmations dipped to 66.2% alongside a newly opened 100-bed Bunia ETC and clinical trial rollouts. (3) Haut-Uele rises 0.15 -> 0.18 as the fastest-growing province by rate (+57.9% in 6d, 38 -> 60 cases, 30 deaths across 5/13 HZs, 458 contacts). (4) Tshopo trims 0.12 -> 0.10 (7 cumulative cases and 65 contacts, though declaring a 5th HZ Wanie-Rukula and lowest contact follow-up at 66.2% preserve Kisangani spillover risk). (5) South Kivu drops 0.02 -> 0.015 (flat at 3 cases since June 10 with zero active contacts; 2.5% residual for Bas-Uele/Maniema/Kinshasa).

local_articles.title: Congo's Ebola outbreak surpasses 4,000 cases
local_articles.snippet: ry's public health institute said in its latest report that the total number of infections had reached 4,053, including 1,850 deaths. Cases have been recorded in five provinces in the country: Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Haut-Uele and Tshopo. A report published in the journal Science last month concluded that Congo's outbreak had started in January, or even earlier, in Ituri. Researchers identified more than 500 suspected cases between mid-January and May 15. Delayed detection, overwhelmed surveillance, military conflict, and a lack of vaccines and treatments for the species of the virus involved have allowed the disease to outrun containment efforts this time. So far only West Africa's 2014-16 outbreak has been bigger, with over 28,000 cases recorded across Guinea, Liberia and Sierra Leone. REUTERS

questions.current_reasoning: World Athletics will award both 2029 and 2031 Championships in September 2026 (final bids due Aug 5); because Tokyo 2025 and Beijing 2027 are both in Asia, 2029 strongly favors Europe or Africa while India's New Delhi bid is better positioned for 2031. London enjoys UK government/mayor backing and proven 2017 sellout pedigree, but Championship club West Ham's unresolved refusal to vacate London Stadium for three weeks in Sept 2029 (still blocked as of late May 2026) trims its probability sharply. That leaves Nairobi (WA Evaluation Panel visited May 2026; historic first African bid with AFCON-upgraded Kasarani), Rome (2024 Euro host), and Munich (2022 Euro host) as formidable contenders.

questions.title: Which club will win the 2026 FA Community Shield?
questions.background: The FA Community Shield is English football's traditional curtain-raiser ahead of the domestic league season.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : The Football Association's official match result or reliable contemporaneous reporting of the result. Resolution Condition : Resolve to the club that wins the 2026 FA Community Shield, including a victory by penalty shootout if applicable. Accepted Answer Format : The winning club's name.
questions.current_reasoning: Multiple major July 22-23 squad and availability updates tilt the August 16 Cardiff curtain-raiser slightly back toward Premier League champions Arsenal (+0.03, from 0.51/0.49 to 0.54/0.46). Both sides suffered major World Cup back-injury blows: Arsenal confirmed on July 22-23 that anchor defender William Saliba is out for an extended period (rehab, no surgery), while July 23 reports (Guardian/Irish Times, The Athletic) confirm City's talisman Rodri faces back surgery ruling him out for the start of the season. Beyond roughly offsetting star absences, Manchester City face sharper early-season transition hurdles: Pep Guardiola has departed with new manager Enzo Maresca making his competitive debut, Bernardo Silva exited to Real Madrid on a free, Phil Foden comes off a 0-goal 2026 slump (though extended to 2030 on July 22), and official £116m record signing Elliot Anderson (announced July 23) will not even join City training until ~August 9 after a three-week post-World Cup break—just one week before kickoff. Meanwhile Arsenal sold Leandro Trossard to Besiktas and walked away from £117m Morgan Rogers (to Chelsea), but completed Belgian Pro League POTY forward Christos Tzolis (£34m, July 23) and are actively bidding £70m for Bruno Guimaraes while retaining Mikel Arteta's title-winning continuity. Keeping Arsenal's edge modest at 54/46 given Saliba's absence, World Cup fatigue for England regulars (Saka, Rice), City's 2026 H2H wins, and straight-to-penalties variance (with Donnarumma in goal).
